definition: Craving, thirst, or desire — in the Buddhist tradition, the force that binds us to suffering by perpetually pulling us toward pleasant experiences and away from unpleasant ones.
Suffering, unsatisfactoriness, or existential dis-ease — the first of the Buddha's Four Noble Truths.
Non-self. The teaching that there is no permanent, unchanging self at the core of one's experience.
Impermanence. The characteristic of all conditioned phenomena constantly arising and passing away.
The cessation of suffering; liberation. Literally 'blown out' or 'extinguished' — the quieting of the fires of craving, aversion, and delusion.
Liberation from the cycle of birth and death; release into one's true nature.
